checks.question: Does our simulator give the published answer?
checks.expect: eating cell (MN9) at 67.0 Hz like Shiu et al.'s own run, within noise (|z| < 3)
checks.why: if our engine disagrees with the published one, nothing built on it can be trusted

checks.question: Does the newer brain map give the same answer?
checks.expect: same 20 sugar cells on the old (v630) and new (v783) map: MN9 rates within noise (|z| < 3)
checks.why: we build on the new map, so it must not change a result the old one got right

checks.question: Does scrambled wiring break the sugar → eating result?
checks.expect: MN9 below 5% of the real wiring's 63.0 Hz
checks.why: if a randomly wired brain also 'eats', the fly's wiring isn't what produces it

checks.question: Does our frame-by-frame stepper match the validated engine?
checks.expect: identical spike counts for every one of the 138,639 neurons, same input
checks.why: the game needs the stepper, so it has to be the same physics, not an approximation

checks.question: With no alarm, does the jump cell stay quiet?
checks.expect: 0 jump-cell spikes when nothing is shown
checks.why: a jump cell that fires on its own would press jump for no reason

checks.question: Do the alarm cells fire at the rate we asked for?
checks.expect: LPLC2 cells at 100 per second, within 5%
checks.why: if the input is wrong, everything measured downstream of it is wrong too

checks.question: Does the alarm make the jump cell fire?
checks.expect: the jump cell fires in all 5 tries at alarm strength 100
checks.got: fired in 5/5 tries, 161 spikes per second
checks.why: this is the escape reflex: no response here means no game

checks.question: Does a stronger alarm give a faster reaction?
checks.expect: time to first jump-cell spike shrinks: strength 25 > 100 > 200
checks.why: the game needs timing that follows how close the spike is

checks.question: With the jump cell switched off, does it stay silent?
checks.expect: 0 jump-cell spikes even at the strongest alarm
checks.why: this is the 'no jump cell' control for the game; the switch has to work

checks.question: Does scrambled wiring break the alarm → jump link?
checks.expect: every one of 5 scrambled brains below 5% of the real wiring's 203 spikes/s at strength 200
checks.got: worst scrambled brain: 0.7 spikes/s (0.3% of real)
checks.why: if a randomly wired brain also jumps, the fly's wiring isn't what makes it jump
